textContent.text: The Golden Gate Bridge is one of the most famous bridges in the world. Its tall frame, two large towers, and orange color make the bridge easy to recognize. Yet as the Golden Gate Bridge was being built, people disagreed about what the bridge should look like.

People were worried that San Francisco's thick fog would make the bridge hard to see. The U.S. Navy wanted the bridge to stand out so ships and airplanes wouldn't collide with it. They wanted the bridge to have wide black and yellow stripes, like a bumblebee! Irving Morrow was one of the bridge designers. He did not like the idea of a striped bridge. Morrow did not want a plain black or gray bridge either, though. He thought a dark bridge would make the Golden Gate seem smaller than it was.

When the bridge's parts were delivered to San Francisco, they had an orange color. The bridge workers were supposed to paint a new color over the orange. But Morrow was still unsure of what color that would be. He looked at the orange bridge parts and decided that the color would be perfect! Morrow thought the orange would stand out well against the ocean and the sky.

Finally, the difficult decision had been made. A red-orange Golden Gate Bridge was bright enough for ships and planes to see. The color made the bridge appear grand and tall. Over the years, fresh paint has been needed. But the color remains the same orange that was supposed to be painted over many years ago.

They wanted the bridge to have wide black and yellow stripes, like a bumblebee! Irving Morrow was one of the bridge designers. He did not like the idea of a striped bridge. Morrow did not want a plain black or gray bridge either, though. He thought a dark bridge would make the Golden Gate seem smaller than it was.

When the bridge's parts were delivered to San Francisco, they had an orange color. The bridge workers were supposed to paint a new color over the orange. But Morrow was still unsure of what color that would be. He looked at the orange bridge parts and decided that the color would be perfect! Morrow thought the orange would stand out well against the ocean and the sky.

Finally, the difficult decision had been made. A red-orange Golden Gate Bridge was bright enough for ships and planes to see. The color made the bridge appear grand and tall. textContent.text: The Panama Canal is a human-made waterway between North and South America. Before the canal was built, ships had to travel around South America to reach the Pacific Ocean from the Atlantic Ocean. The new waterway through the country of Panama created an easier route for ships. However, building the Panama Canal turned out to be harder than anyone expected.

In the late 1800s, France tried to build a canal through Panama. The country had thick jungles, though. This caused workers to suffer a lot. There were poisonous snakes, insects, and spiders in the jungle. Heavy jungle rains also caused many accidents for the workers. Worst of all, mosquito bites caused yellow fever and other illnesses. But nobody knew the mosquitoes were to blame. So, the workers kept getting sick. Because of these hazards, France stopped working on the canal. It wasn't safe for the workers.

In 1902, the United States decided to try to build the Panama Canal. John Stevens was put in charge of the project. Stevens improved the safety of the workers, so there were fewer accidents. He also improved workers' housing. The new housing helped protect workers from the dangerous mosquitoes. Dr. William Gorgas was also brought to Panama to help with mosquitoes. Gorgas's team used special sprays to kill the mosquitoes. The team also put mosquito netting around the workers' houses. After two years, there were almost no cases of mosquito-caused illnesses at the canal site.

Because of the efforts of Stevens and Gorgas, the Panama Canal finally opened in 1914. Since then, hundreds of thousands of ships have passed through the canal. It has helped move people and goods quickly between countries. Even so, the Panama Canal is still remembered as one of the hardest projects in history.

textContent.text: The Waitomo Caves are one of the most famous places to visit in New Zealand. Each year, around half a million people visit the caves. Why do so many people visit these caves? It's because they are so different from other caves around the world.

From bat dens in Texas to sinkholes in Australia, caves are usually dark places. The Waitomo Caves don't follow this rule, though. The Waitomo Caves are lit up by thousands of small bugs that glow in the dark. These glowworms line the cave walls and ceiling, filling the caves with a soft blue-green light. Because of this light, people can see the beautiful rock formations throughout the caves.

The glowworms that line the cave are not actually worms—they're baby flies. The baby flies begin glowing bright blue soon after they hatch from eggs in the cave. They use this light to attract other bugs that are lost in the cave. When the lost bugs see the light, they go toward it. Then the glowworms can catch the bugs and eat them. And when the glowworms are very hungry, they can shine their lights even brighter to catch even more bugs.

The glowworms have made the Waitomo Caves a must-see stop on any vacation to New Zealand. You can hike through the caves or take a slow-moving boat ride through them. The natural glow of the caves shows how magical nature can be. If you're ever in New Zealand, you may want to check these caves out!

The tower had been badly damaged over time, and the duke wanted the damage to be fixed. Under his order, a new staircase was built inside the tower. The staircase allowed people to once again reach the top of the tower. Two new lights were placed in the top of the tower to light the way for ships. In the early 1900s, the lights were replaced with electric ones. These lights still shine in the tower today.

People were worried that San Francisco's thick fog would make the bridge hard to see. The U.S. Navy wanted the bridge to stand out so ships and airplanes wouldn't collide with it. They wanted the bridge to have wide black and yellow stripes, like a bumblebee! Irving Morrow was one of the bridge designers. He did not like the idea of a striped bridge. Morrow did not want a plain black or gray bridge either, though. He thought a dark bridge would make the Golden Gate seem smaller than it was.

When the bridge's parts were delivered to San Francisco, they had an orange color. The bridge workers were supposed to paint a new color over the orange. But Morrow was still unsure of what color that would be. He looked at the orange bridge parts and decided that the color would be perfect! Morrow thought the orange would stand out well against the ocean and the sky.

Finally, the difficult decision had been made. A red-orange Golden Gate Bridge was bright enough for ships and planes to see. The color made the bridge appear grand and tall. textContent.text: Sandy Island was first discovered by a whaling ship in 1876. It was found in the Coral Sea, off the east coast of Australia. Soon after that, many maps and sailing charts included Sandy Island. These maps and charts helped traders and explorers navigate the waters. The problem is that no one today can actually find Sandy Island.

The puzzling story of Sandy Island was brought to the world's attention by scientist Maria Seton. In the fall of 2012, she was leading a team of researchers through the Coral Sea. They were collecting samples of rocks from the ocean floor. Her maps showed that her ship should have been right next to Sandy Island. However, there was no land in sight. Seton was looking at maps made by experts. How could so many maps be wrong?

Seton tried to figure out the puzzle. Her work led to an idea for how the island first came to be on maps. The Coral Sea has some underwater volcanoes. When lava bursts from the ocean floor, it can create large floating rocks. Over time, these enormous rocks break apart and disappear. But sometimes, they can float for several years before disappearing. Floating rocks have been spotted in the area where Sandy Island supposedly stood. So, sailors on early ships may have mistaken the rocks for an island. This could explain why the island first appeared on maps.

Still, until 2012, many major maps had Sandy Island existing as surely as Australia. It took one ocean researcher to make the puzzle of Sandy Island widely known. Maria Seton's discovery shows us that, even today, the ocean still has plenty of mysteries.
